# Carry named Neo MCP approvals in the Codex template

## Context

The operator requested one common Codex MCP approval baseline for the GPT peers on 2026-10-07. Parsed comparison found 74 explicit named-tool `approval_mode = "approve"` entries in the approved local baseline and the active Emmy config, but none in the tracked `.codex/config.template.toml`: GitHub Workflow 21, Knowledge Base 7, Memory Core 21, Neural Link 25.

Design authority: @tobiu requested that the additions reach the non-ignored template because all GPT peers should have the same allowances.

## The Problem

A new setup copied from the shared template loses the named tool policy already approved for the team's local configs. Repeating private config edits leaves future peers without a reproducible repository baseline.

## The Architectural Reality

`.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` (Codex setup) directs users to copy `.codex/config.template.toml` into ignored `.codex/config.toml`. The template owns the repository bootstrap defaults; live ignored configs remain local. Brain's Fleet project-config generator is a separate producer and is not changed here.

Prescription checked: `.codex/config.template.toml` owns this concern, confirmed by an independent read of its quick-start consumer. The Brain structure map completed; no new Agent OS source location or module is introduced.

## The Fix

Add exactly the operator-approved 74 named-tool entries as Codex MCP tool sub-tables, grouped by their existing server. Preserve every existing setting outside those additions. Explain that unlisted/new tools retain the client default.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Edge | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp_servers.<server>.tools.<tool>.approval_mode` in the tracked template | Operator's named 74-tool baseline | Explicit `approve` for those tool identities | No wildcard or implicit approval of later tools | Brief template comment | TOML parse and exact-set comparison |
| Existing transport, authentication, context, sandbox and features settings | Current template | Unchanged | No live config or credential copied | Existing quick-start remains valid | Parsed before/after comparison excluding added tool tables |

## Decision Record impact

None: carries an explicitly authorized repository policy into its existing bootstrap template; no runtime service or AiConfig contract changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The template parses as TOML and contains exactly 74 named approvals: GH 21 / KB 7 / MC 21 / NL 25, each matching the approved baseline.
- [ ] Removing those added tool tables yields parsed settings identical to the previous template, with existing comments and placeholders preserved.
- [ ] No wildcard, additional tool identity, credential, machine-specific path, global approval-mode change, or sandbox change is introduced.
- [ ] Existing ignored configs and Fleet's generated configuration are not rewritten by this change.

## Out of Scope

Fleet settings import, live profile edits, memory recovery, hook approval, model/effort selection and PR merging.

## Related and creation evidence

Related outcome: neomjs/neo-agent-brain#571; this does not close its settings-import gap. Live latest-20 Engine open issues and the current A2A slice were checked immediately before filing; no equivalent or overlapping claim found. Exact `approval_mode` issue search and KB ticket search found no equivalent. Memory Core rationale queries returned adjacent onboarding history, not this policy-template change. Own assignments: two Engine issues, neither on this surface.
